title: Meeting the Transport Needs of Singaporeans
what_it_is: Meeting the Transport Needs of Singaporeans

sections.label: Land use and transport emissions
sections.summary: Roads occupy 12% of land, industry 13% and housing 15%, while land transport accounts for about 15% of domestic carbon emissions.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr S Iswaran)
sentences.text: Roads occupy 12% of our land, compared to around 13% for industry and 15% for housing.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr S Iswaran)
sentences.text: Our land transport system accounts for about 15% of Singapore's total domestic carbon emissions.

sections.label: Rail network journeys and area
sections.summary: The rail network serves around three million journeys a day and takes up less than 1% of total surface area.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr S Iswaran)
sentences.text: Our rail network serves around three million journeys a day and takes up less than 1% of our total surface area.

sections.label: Additional rail kilometres being built
sections.summary: An additional 100 km of rail is being built, almost a 40% increase from the current rail network.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr S Iswaran)
sentences.text: To achieve this, we are building an additional 100 kilometres (km) of rail, almost a 40% increase from our current rail network.

sections.label: Island-wide cycling path network growth
sections.summary: By 2030, the island-wide cycling path network will more than double to about 1,300 km.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr S Iswaran)
sentences.text: By 2030, the island-wide cycling path network will more than double to about 1,300 km.

sections.label: Youths' car ownership aspirations
sections.summary: A Straits Times survey found the percentage of youths aspiring to own a car fell from around 65% in 2016 to around 50% in 2022.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr S Iswaran)
sentences.text: According to a Straits Times survey, the percentage of youths who aspire to own a car has fallen from around 65% in 2016 to around 50% in 2022.

sections.label: Cat A and Cat B car OMV
sections.summary: Between 2018 and April this year, the median OMV for Cat A cars each year was just over half that of Cat B cars.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr S Iswaran)
sentences.text: On Mr Leong Mun Wai's question, between 2018 and April this year, the median Open Market Value, or OMV, for Cat A cars for each year was just over half of the median OMV for Cat B cars in the same year.

sections.label: Expired Cat D TCOEs
sections.summary: About 450 Cat D TCOEs secured at prices near or above $13,000 were left to expire when COE prices fell.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr S Iswaran)
sentences.text: As I explained at my Ministry’s Committee of Supply (COS) debate this year, about 450 Cat D TCOEs that were secured when prices were close to or above $13,000, were subsequently left to expire when COE prices fell.

sections.label: Higher bid deposit, shorter TCOE validity
sections.summary: Bid deposit was raised from $800 to $1,500 and TCOE validity shortened from three months to one month.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr S Iswaran)
sentences.text: Nevertheless, to improve allocative efficiency and deter any speculative bidding, we made further moves recently, to increase the bid deposit from $800 to $1,500 and to shorten the TCOE validity period from three months to one month.

sections.label: Car-owning households in Singapore
sections.summary: As of 31 October 2022, 471,000 households owned cars, about 36% of all households; 12% owned two cars and under 3% owned three or more.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr S Iswaran)
sentences.text: In November last year, I had shared with this House that as of 31 October 2022, of the 471,000 households that own cars – and that is about 36% of all households in Singapore – 12% own two cars, and less than 3% own three or more cars.

sections.label: COE prices reflect limited supply
sections.summary: COE prices reflect demand for a limited supply, exacerbated by being at a trough in the 10-year COE supply cycle.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr S Iswaran)
sentences.text: Fundamentally, the COE prices reflect demand for a limited supply of COEs.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr S Iswaran)
sentences.text: This is further accentuated or exacerbated by the fact that we are now at a trough in the 10-year cycle of COE supply.

sections.label: Redistributing five-year COE supply
sections.summary: LTA will bring forward and redistribute five-year COE supply due to expire, raising the next bidding exercise quota by about 24% in Cat A and 15% in Cat B.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr S Iswaran)
sentences.text: Consequently, as a one-off exercise, LTA will bring forward and redistribute the supply from five-year COEs which are due to expire in the next projected supply peak.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr S Iswaran)
sentences.text: This supply will be redistributed over several quarters starting from the next bidding exercise.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr S Iswaran)
sentences.text: This move will increase quota supply in the next bidding exercise by about 24% in Cat A and 15% in Cat B.

sections.label: Evolving transport needs and policies
sections.summary: As Singapore develops, Singaporeans' transport needs will evolve and transport policies must move in tandem while paying heed to key constraints.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr S Iswaran)
sentences.text: As Singapore develops and grows, Singaporeans’ transport needs will continue to evolve and our transport policies must move in tandem while paying heed to our key constraints.

sections.label: COE cash payment and bidding
sections.summary: The COE must be paid in cash, and the current auction method is described as probably the most efficient.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak (Sembawang)
sentences.text: The COE has to be paid in cash.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: But if I may, say, first, a pay-as-you-bid system, I understand the motivation behind it.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: But if I may offer Members the counterpoint – the problem then is you create a great deal of variation in the market.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: For the same car bought in the same exercise, the value may be quite different because one bids higher and one bids lower.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: I do not want to get into a long discussion on this, but from an auction theory perspective and so on, actually the method we use is probably the most efficient.

sections.label: COE and car indivisible
sections.summary: A COE and the car are indivisible.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: A COE and the car are indivisible, really.

sections.label: Balloted and non-balloted COEs
sections.summary: If some COEs are balloted and the rest are not, one segment is secured by bidding and another by luck of the draw.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: If we say a proportion of COEs are balloted and the rest are not, then the question is: so, we have a market where you bid and you secure; and then, there is another segment which is by luck of the draw, literally.

sections.label: Populating commuting choices
sections.summary: Populating the spectrum of commuting choices, including public transport, car sharing and P2P services, may lead people to re-evaluate car purchases.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: The most important thing that we need to do is to populate the spectrum of commuting choices available to Singaporeans.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: The more we are able to offer a high-quality public transport system and near-car kind of services, whether it is car sharing, your P2Ps and so on, and if we can also make the first-mile last-mile part of the commute a better one, then I think people who choose to pay the sum that they pay, or the sums that they pay to buy a car, will have reason to take a pause and re-evaluate the choices that they make.

sections.label: Electrification of public bus fleet
sections.summary: Sustainability is sought mainly through electrification, with about half of the 6,000 public buses electric by 2030 and the other half hybrid.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: The main way we are seeking to ensure sustainability is through electrification.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: We have about 6,000 buses in the public bus fleet.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: And about half of these will be electric by 2030; the other half will be a hybrid solution.

sections.label: Alternative vehicle quota allocation
sections.summary: The Minister is asked whether alternative ways of allocating the vehicle quota based on other factors, instead of just price alone, would be considered.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Would the Minister consider alternative ways of allocating the vehicle quota based on other factors, instead of just price alone?

sections.label: Targeted help for vehicle costs
sections.summary: The market is left to work, with targeted schemes helping people with special needs or disability with vehicle costs including COEs.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: We are trying to let the market work itself through.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: We do have schemes where we help people – for example, those who have special needs or persons with disability who need vehicles for, say, work and so on, we do have schemes to help them with that, including with the COEs and so on.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: Those are very targeted measures that we can do, but that is best achieved not by tinkering with the COE allocation system, but by, instead, trying to defray some, if not all, of the cost impact on certain groups.

sections.label: Alternatives to car ownership
sections.summary: Targeted measures and car-sharing services exist, letting households use a car for hours and saving money versus buying a car.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: Having said that, we are working on and, in fact, we do have some alternatives, as I have said, for persons with disability and so on, we have got certain targeted measures.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: Also, car-sharing services, because these allow households to have a car for a few hours to do what they need to do and then come back and leave the car for somebody else to use.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: So, that actually is a more efficient outcome and, in fact, it would save households a lot more money than buying a car and incurring the depreciation.

sections.label: ABSD and COE prices
sections.summary: The COE price today is not explained by multiple car-owning households.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: As far as the idea of ABSD is concerned, I have already pointed out clearly that the COE price that we see today is not explained by multiple car-owning households.

sections.label: Progressivity in COE system
sections.summary: Significant progressivity already exists through the tax system and the ARF system for cars.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: If the Member's intent is that we should have progressivity in the COE system, actually, we already have significant progressivity through the tax system, the ARF system that we have today, in terms of cars.

sections.label: Transition to car-lite
sections.summary: The transition is not just to car-lite, as it takes at least about 10 more years for good MRT connectivity in many parts.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: The transition is not just in terms of going to car-lite, but also because it would take us at least about 10 years more before our MRT system comes to that level where we really have good connectivity in many parts.

sections.label: Five-year COE redeployment
sections.summary: Five-year COEs expiring in about three or four years will be redeployed over the next few quarters, leading up to a peak.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: Essentially, we have got five-year COEs that will expire probably in about three- or four-years' time and that is when you are really going to know, if you look at the historical cycles, there is going to be a sort of peak-ish.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: So, that is where LTA is basically extracting the five-year COEs from.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: And these will be redeployed – in not just this quarter, the next quarter but in the next few quarters at least, leading up to this.

sections.label: COE supply and speculative bidding
sections.summary: The speaker says the objective is to smoothen supply and reduce volatility, and that the Minister now recognises speculative bidding by dealers as a factor.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: The objective here is to smoothen the supply, reduce the volatility so that people can then make their choices.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: I think the Minister will know I have spoken on this a number of times, including on 1 March where I asked for more measures to deter speculative bidding.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: And I think what the Minister mentioned about the main measures suggests that he now recognises that, beyond supply and demand, speculative behaviour by dealers who have the incentives to bid up prices actually is a factor, and especially so, it is amplified in a market where we are talking about a few hundred COEs every month.

sections.label: Dealer deposits and motorcycle bidding
sections.summary: The speaker suggests tying dealer deposits to bid size and allowing individuals to bid for motorcycles as for cars.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: One suggestion could be – I mean $200, $800, $1,500, it is a bit arbitrary.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Could we tie the dealer deposits to the size of their bids, to be a bit quicker to rein in speculative bidding?

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Two, could we allow for individuals to bid, like we have for cars, for motorcycles also?

sections.label: PHC to private car conversions
sections.summary: The speaker asks how many cars are converted from PHCs to private cars by platform companies as an option.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: How many cars are converted from PHCs to private cars by these platform companies as an option?

sections.label: Forfeited supply and validity period
sections.summary: The speaker states that before the latest move, such as reducing the validity period, forfeited supply could not return to the market until the next quarter.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: What happens then is, just to be very clear, before we made the latest move, such as the reduction of the validity period, was that the supply that is forfeited cannot be returned to the market until the next quarter.

sections.label: Deposit amount comparison with cars
sections.summary: The speaker says $1,500 is about 10% or so, of a similar order of magnitude to COEs for cars.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: If you take $1,500, for example, it is something like – well, at least before this recent correction which may or may not be sustained – but it is about 10% or so and it is of a similar order of magnitude to what we have for COEs for cars.

sections.label: PHC growth and COE prices
sections.summary: The speaker says PHC population doubling from 2015 to 2017 had no particularly discernible impact on COE prices, while recent COE price rises came as PHC demand moderated.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: Basically, in the period, for example, 2015 to 2017, when the PHC population grew from 30,000 to 70,000 or nearly 70,000, so doubling, the impact on COE prices was not particularly discernible.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: By the same token, and conversely, over the last several quarters and years, COE prices have been rising but, actually, PHC demand or the number of COEs PHCs have secured has actually been moderating.

sections.label: Bus service rationalisation savings
sections.summary: MP asks if productivity gains are all MOT expects and how bus service rationalisation savings reach commuters.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Are these all the productivity gains that MOT is expecting the PTOs to achieve and could that be too low an expectation?

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: And lastly, when PTOs rationalise bus services – for example, the removal of bus services 22, 66 and 506 for my residents in Bedok Reservoir in 2022 and 2021, sorry I am not letting go of this – which saves the Government $9.5 million a year in subsidies, how are these cost savings passed to commuters?

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: First, the formula – I think it is important to understand that 0.1% is a productivity contribution, but it is a deduction from the fare increase.

sections.label: Bus subsidies and savings
sections.summary: Member says bus services are subsidised a billion dollars a year, addressing how savings pass to commuters.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: On the Member's point on rationalising bus services and, when there are savings, how does it get passed through to commuters?

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: So, if I may, like the Member, persevere and persist with my counterpoints, the fact is that we are subsidising bus services a billion dollars a year.

sections.label: Bus and train subsidies
sections.summary: A billion dollars each for bus and train, or a $1 subsidy per journey.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: A billion dollars for bus, a billion dollars for train, or, if you want to think about it in another way, every journey gets a $1 subsidy.

sections.label: One-off five-year COE exercise
sections.summary: Measures would be fair, a one-off exercise with a five-year time horizon because of the five-year COE.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Any measures to help do that would be fair.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: It is a one-off exercise and, specifically, because it is a five-year COE, the time horizon is five years.

sections.label: Smoothening and supply category
sections.summary: It is a good time to look at smoothening, which is why this is adopted, and supply returns to the relevant category.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: So, it is a good time to look at how we can do some smoothening and this is the reason we are adopting this.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: And, yes, the supply will go back to the relevant category.

sections.label: Cat A and B to Cat E
sections.summary: Of Cat A and Cat B, 10% goes into Cat E.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: Of Cat A and Cat B, 10% goes into Cat E, alright?

sections.label: COE contribution valve throttled
sections.summary: The system acts as a valve that has been progressively throttled down, with contribution from different categories now at 10%.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: So, this really creates a valve in the system.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: It is a valve that we have actually been progressively throttling down.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: In fact, in the early days, it was much more – the contribution from the different categories – and today it is 10%.

sections.label: MAS loan restrictions purpose
sections.summary: MAS restrictions on loans by financial institutions aim to encourage borrowers to spend or borrow prudently.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
sentences.text: So, I will respond for MAS using that PQ.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
sentences.text: But, primarily, MAS' restrictions on loans that are granted by financial institutions are to encourage borrowers to spend or to borrow prudently.

sections.label: Cat E COE contribution from Cat C
sections.summary: Cat E COE contribution comes from 10% of deregistered Cats A, B and C, shrinking Cat C COEs for commercial vehicles.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (West Coast)
sentences.text: As what the Minister has said, the contribution of Cat E COE is from 10% of deregistered Cats A, B and C.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (West Coast)
sentences.text: I want to ask the Minister why do we want to contribute from Cat C where it is mainly used for commercial vehicles and all the Cat E COEs are mainly to register Cat B COE, which means that you are shrinking the Cat C COEs meant for commercial vehicles.

sections.label: Five-year COEs brought to present
sections.summary: Other vehicles are in the same class and contribution group, bringing expiring five-year COEs to the present.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: But for all the other vehicles, they are in the same class and we put them in that contribution group.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: This is already a big move – taking five-year COEs that are expiring in the future and bringing them to the present.

sections.label: COE re-allocation and supply increase
sections.summary: Re-allocation returns Cat A to Cat A and Cat B to Cat B, increasing current bidding quarter supply by 24%, with Cat B five-year COEs lower.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: But we just want to have a situation where we do not make too many arbitrary kind of decisions.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: So, in response to Mr Vikram Nair's question earlier, I said we will re-allocate on this basis, that Cat A will come back to Cat A, Cat B to Cat B.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: As I said earlier in my Ministerial Statement, for the bidding quarter we are having now, it will increase supply by 24%.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: In fact, the five-year COEs that are available for Cat B, we are a lot less and that is why also, consequently, you see a much lower percentage increase of about 15%.

sections.label: OMV criterion for Cat A
sections.summary: A grievance is that expensive cars are going to Cat A, so the Minister is asked to consider OMV as an additional criterion for Cat A.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: So, one of the grievances that I have also heard from some residents is that the Cat A and Cat B, a lot of the expensive cars are now going down to Cat A.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: So, as a result, in order to ensure more equity amongst Singaporeans – the lower-income can still buy cars, the cheaper cars – will the Minister consider putting OMV as an additional criterion for classifying Cat A?

sections.label: No price or range stipulated
sections.summary: The Minister states categorically that no price or even a price range is being stipulated.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: If I can take the Member's second question first.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: I want to put that categorically on the table because we are not stipulating the price or even a range.

sections.label: Market equilibrium and upward price pressure
sections.summary: Industry players advocate watching the situation while the market finds a new equilibrium, with long-term upward price pressure expected.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: I think even if you listen to the industry players, they would advocate that we watch this for a while because whether it is buyers or dealers, they all have to sort of assess the situation and the market will have to find a new equilibrium.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: But what I can say with certainty is that, in the long term, we will see upward price pressure for the fundamental realities we have discussed.

sections.label: Median OMV Cat B versus Cat A
sections.summary: The median OMV for Cat B is about 70% to 75% more than the median OMV for Cat A.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: The median OMV for Cat B is about 70%, 75% more than the median OMV for Cat A.

sections.label: Reviewing category criteria, not OMV
sections.summary: The criteria dividing the two categories will be reviewed if needed, but there is no compelling reason now, and not to use OMV.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: And that is why we have two categories.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: And, as I said in my Ministerial Statement, we will continue to look at this and if there is a need to adjust the criteria that divide the two categories, we will look at it.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: But as of now, there is no compelling reason and, certainly, not to use the OMV.

sections.label: Fundamental constraints and transport system goals
sections.summary: The objective is for the House and Singaporeans to understand fundamental constraints around land and carbon emissions, and to work on other options for an accessible, inclusive, sustainable transport system.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: The objective, if I may restate, with your indulgence, Mr Deputy Speaker, is that we need to make sure that all of us in this House and Singaporeans in general understand the fundamental constraints that we are dealing with.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: We cannot run away from them and those constraints around land, around carbon emissions and what we need to do are something that we will have to grapple with.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: Previous Transport Ministers have had to do this, I am doing it, future Transport Ministers will have to do this.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: But, in the end, they need this House to support and also the broader society because if we do not internalise these constraints, then we are always going to be unhappy with the outcome.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: What we do need to do though is then work on all the other options and solutions so that we can make the transport system in Singapore not just car-lite but, as I have said, accessible and inclusive and sustainable.
